description:
`ai` answers an OpenAI chat request with the AI you've chosen as your AI preference: a `/p/llm` tier or another LLM service anyone on your account can call.

The gateway rewrites `/ai/...` to your preference, the way it rewrites an `/a/<name>` alias, then routes it like any other call, streaming included. The preference names one service: a `/p/llm` tier, an LLM service from the marketplace, or one of your aliases. A service is one model, so the app never picks the model. Services that require enrollment are refused, including `e/<code>` enrollments and services (or aliases pointing at them) that can only be reached through an enrollment, because an enrollment brings its own parameters and model choices. With none set, `/ai` uses `labs/llm-balanced` (`/p/llm`, `model="balanced"`). A team key uses the team's own preference, or that default billed to the team, never a member's personal one. A key may override the preference: its `service:ai` grant's `service` option names a catalog service (never an alias or enrollment) that the key's `/ai` calls use instead, under the same rules. If the saved preference or the grant's service no longer resolves (a deleted alias, or a service that now requires enrollment), `/ai` answers 409 instead of silently using the default. `ai` itself is free: each call is billed by the service it resolves to, at that service's own price.

Point any OpenAI-compatible client at `/ai` with your UnitySVC key, and set your AI under **Your AI** in Preferences (or `PUT /v1/preferences/ai`). Switch provider or model there, without changing the app. To pin one app's key to a specific AI, give it a `service:ai` grant with `invoke` and, for example, the option `service=labs/llm-premium`; the response's `X-UnitySVC-AI-Scope` header is then `grant`.

service.description: The catalog service this grant's /ai calls use instead of your AI preference, by its catalog name (labs/llm-premium, openai/gpt-5). It must be an active LLM service that accepts OpenAI chat requests and needs no enrollment; aliases (a/...), enrollments (e/...) and /ai itself are refused. Unset uses your (or your team's) AI preference.
service.title: AI service

name: ai

payout_price.description: No platform commission — each call is billed by the AI service it resolves to

summary: Send an OpenAI chat request to `/ai` and UnitySVC answers it with the AI you've chosen — a `/p/llm` tier or another LLM service — with no service or model to hard-code.
